transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-03-10
Time: 15:00 PST
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Patel (Redwood AE), Marcus Li (Redwood SE), Jordan Mills (Redwood Partnerships), Daniel Kim (NimbleTech AM), Priya Rao (NimbleTech SE), Lena Ortiz (NimbleTech Sales)

Summary: Quick partner pipeline review across three active deals (Brightline Health, Acme Retail, Zephyr IoT). Focus on next steps for co-sell motions, benchmarks for performance/latency, and clarifying margin splits and responsibility for outreach. Some discussion of security/Private deployment for Brightline.

Topics: pipeline status, technical blockers, benchmarking, pricing splits, GTM activities, upcoming exec engagement

-- Transcript --
[00:00] Sofia: hey everyone, thanks for joining. uh, we'll run through the pipeline items, quick status, any blockers, and decide next steps. daniel, you want to kick us off with Brightline?
[00:18] Daniel: yeah thanks sofia. Brightline's probably the top priority, they're... they're in final app evaluation for, uh, virtual care triage. we did the initial PoC last month. they liked the latency and response quality but, um, there's questions around VPC and data residency and they asked about a private deploy option.
[00:38] Marcus: hi, this is marcus. on the tech side the PoC ran on Redwood Dedicated and we saw consistent 120-160ms p95 on 1k token scenarios, but when we tried a local on-prem run the KV cache warmup added some overhead. also i want to flag, the customer's infra team asked about audit logs and KMS integration.
[01:02] Priya: yep, nimble's SE here, we mapped that — Brightline cares about SOC 2 and needs a KMS/HSM integration for keys. they asked if Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS, and if logs can be pushed to their SIEM.
[01:20] Sofia: correct — we do support KMS integrations and audit trails, though for private deployments there's a bit of lead time. i'll follow up with the security doc. marcus, can you capture which exact artifacts we need to send?
[01:33] Marcus: sure. i'll add the security checklist and a short runbook for the private deploy. expect that by thursday.
[01:40] Lena: also, Brightline is worried about price. their procurement asked for a dedicated commit estimate vs hosted pay-as-you-go, and they want a rough TCO for 12 months.
[01:54] Sofia: okay, on pricing — nimble and us have to agree on margin share for co-sell. jordan, you're the partnerships lead, any constraints?
[02:03] Jordan: yeah, from partners side nimble is asking for a 20% referral margin on net new ARR for the first 12 months. i think that's in the ballpark but we need to map to Redwood's committed pricing for Dedicated.
[02:18] Sofia: perfect. we'll draft an updated co-sell pricing sheet. daniel, can you confirm Brightline's expected commit level?
[02:25] Daniel: they're targeting a 350k annual run rate if the pilot scales. but initial commit will be smaller — probably 50k monthly for the first quarter.
[02:35] Sofia: good. Marcus, get us the Dedicated vs Hosted unit costs so we can show TCO.
[02:41] Marcus: will do. i'll include batching and quantization options, cost per token numbers, and expected latency impact.
[02:49]
[03:00] Sofia: next up Acme Retail. where are we?
[03:05] Daniel: acme's in discovery still. nimble's had two outbound meetings; they want a demo of multi-tenant cart recovery use case. acme's merchant platform is sensitive to latency; they asked about edge routing and region placement.
[03:22] Priya: technical contact at acme cares about our streaming latency and fallback. they asked if Redwood can do regional routing and fallback to a lower-cost variant if capacity is constrained.
[03:35] Marcus: yes, that's Smart routing — sorry, the term was, um, smart routing — it routes by policy and can fallback to compatible model variants. latency numbers will vary by region, we should run a quick benchmark from their region.
[03:48] Lena: acme also asked if there are prebuilt connectors for their CRM.
[03:52] Jordan: nimble will handle the CRM integration piece but we should supply the API docs. Sofia, can we prepare a joint demo for acme next Tuesday?
[03:59] Sofia: i think tues 3/18 looks good, we'll tentatively block it. action: nimble to confirm availability, we will prepare demo script.
[04:10]
[04:22] Sofia: last deal — Zephyr IoT, larger but longer cycle. status?
[04:26] Daniel: zephyr is more interesting but requires private deployment and some custom kernel optimization. they are also evaluating inferex and majorcloud's managed offering.
[04:36] Marcus: from a perf standpoint, zephyr's workloads are long-context summaries and we need to test continuous batching. we can propose a quantized model variant to reduce costs.
[04:48] Priya: zephyr's security team pushed back on open model sharing; they'll need stricter egress controls.
[04:54] Sofia: understood. let's treat Zephyr as a longer-term play — prioritize Brightline and Acme.
[05:02]
[05:10] Marcus: quick note: the Brightline PoC transcripts had a few artifacts — sometimes the transcript errors on named entities. in the report i'll tag where human review changed things.
[05:22] Daniel: thanks. also for the benchmarking — do we run Redwood Dedicated in nimble's cloud region or run from our hosted region? they'd prefer to see performance in their infra.
[05:33] Marcus: we can spin a Dedicated instance in their cloud region but that'll require scheduling and capacity reservation. if they want on-prem, there's extra lead time.
[05:44] Lena: procurement asked for SLA numbers. do we have a document with p95 latency SLOs and uptime guarantees for Dedicated?
[05:54] Jordan: yes, we have the Dedicated SLA pack. jordan to share link — i'll post in the notes.
[06:02] Sofia: ok let's move into specifics — who owns what and due dates.
[06:08] Daniel: i'll coordinate the Brightline exec intro; we can aim for next week Wed/Thu. i'll confirm by Friday.
[06:16] Sofia: great. Marcus — benchmark by 3/17. Jordan — share co-sell pricing template by 3/13. Priya — tech brief for Acme by 3/16.
[06:26] Priya: noted, will do.
[06:30]
[06:40] Sofia: competitors — Brightline mentioned Anthropic and OpenAI as alternatives; they'd like to see our cost and quality comparison. Marcus, can you prepare a short slide comparing our latencies and cost per 1k tokens vs those options?
[06:53] Marcus: yes, i'll do that and caveat with model version differences. might be some variance.
[06:59]
[07:10] Daniel: one more ask: nimble wants a joint customer reference for a similar healthcare customer. do you have a reference?
[07:17] Sofia: we have a reference in midwest telehealth that did a similar deployment last year — i'll check permission to share.
[07:25] Daniel: ok that would help.
[07:28]
[07:40] Lena: procurement also flagged compliance — ISO 27001, SOC2. they want to receive the certs.
[07:49] Jordan: i'll attach the security pack and certs.
[07:52]
[08:00] Sofia: cool. any blockers we didn't capture?
[08:04] Priya: for Acme, we need a short demo script showing cart recovery flow and expected concurrency. other than that nothing major.
[08:13] Sofia: good. final recap:
[08:18] Sofia: Brightline — Marcus run perf benchmark in customer's region vs hosted, include KMS/audit docs (Marcus); Daniel to coordinate exec intro; Sofia to update pricing spreadsheet and share co-sell margins (Sofia & Jordan).
[08:33] Sofia: Acme — joint demo 3/18 tentative; Priya to prepare tech brief; nimble to handle CRM integration and outreach.
[08:43] Sofia: Zephyr — lower priority, longer cycle, need on-prem plan for kernel optimizations (Marcus + Priya).
[08:51]
[08:55] Marcus: i'll also include a short note on fallback behavior and model variants and the expected latency delta when quantization is used.
[09:03] Daniel: perfect.
[09:05] Sofia: ok thanks everyone. we'll send notes and action items after this. meeting adjourned.

Recorded notes & links referenced: co-sell-pricing.xlsx (link shared in chat), Dedicated-SLA.pdf (link), security_pack_v2.zip (link), Brightline PoC report (link)
